chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said:
The divorce of a bondwoman is through her sale or the sale of her husband.
And he said regarding a man who marries his bondwoman to a free man and then sells her: this is separation between them, unless the purchaser wishes to leave them together.

key_terms.الْمُشْتَرِي: the buyer; the purchaser who acquires ownership
key_terms.بَيْعُهَا: her sale; transfer of ownership of the bondwoman
key_terms.زَوْجِهَا: her husband; the man to whom she is married
key_terms.فِرَاقُ: separation; termination of the marital bond
key_terms.يَدَعَهُمَا: to leave them; to allow the couple to remain together

ai.seo_question: Does the sale of a bondwoman affect her marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the marital status of a bondwoman when ownership changes through sale. It states that the sale of the bondwoman, or the sale of her husband, effects separation, while in one case the buyer may choose to maintain the marriage.
